title: BLOOD GLUCOSE MONITORING BY FINGER PRICK
knowledge: Discusses definition of Blood Glucose Monitoring.
Identify purpose and indications of blood glucose monitoring.
Discusses the proper step of blood glucose monitoring by finger prick.
skills: Doctor's order is checked and reviewed.
Assemble the necessary supplies and equipment.
Explained the procedure to the patient.
Hand washing is done, disposable gloves are worn.
Wipes patient's finger to be lanced with alcohol swab and dries thoroughly.
Turned glucometer machine on and verified the meter calibration with strips to be used: Checked the meter readiness for testing blood sugar.
Pricked the patient's finger lateral to the fingertip using lancet.
Applies ample amount of blood to the strip test using standard precaution.
Covers the pricked finger with cotton or gauze until bleeding subsides.
Complete the test and records the result.
Blood contaminated items are disposed properly: Used sharps or needles are discarded in a punctured resistant container.
attitude: Accept constrictive criticism as learning opportunity.
To be self-aware of limitation in knowledge and skills.
To be approachable and open to answer patients and family's questions.
Attentive to overall patient experience e.g. pain, anxiety and have ability to provide comfort and emotional support as needed.

Ability to organize and facilitate a Reflection session in and on practice after Blood Glucose Monitoring by Finger Prick learning opportunity occurs and activates findings to improve future practice and response.

title: ADMINISTRATION OF BLOOD AND BLOOD PRODUCTS
knowledge: State the rationale of blood and blood products administration And check physician order and ensure patient has been cross matched as per policy.
Explore the importance of checking the physician order and ensuring that the patient has been grouped and cross matched as per policy prior to order being written.
Discuss the patient's rights to refuse the administration of blood and blood products.
Describe the process of collecting blood and blood products from the transfusion center.
Describe the completion of the independent double check process, monitoring time, and documentation.
Discuss pre, ongoing and post patient assessment during blood and blood products administration.
Discuss the rationale and importance of making sure that the blood and plasma do not remain separated during administration.
Discuss the role of the nurse and action to be taken when the blood and plasma separates during administration.
Verbalizes signs and symptoms a patient may have as a result of a reaction to the administration of blood and blood products.
State the nurse's role and responsibility when a reaction is identified.
State the process to be used when blood and blood products collected from transfusion center is not used for any reason.
Discuss the correct storage of blood and blood products.
Discuss the documentation needed for the administration of blood and blood products.
skills: Demonstrate checking physician order and ensuring that patient has been cross matched as per policy.
Demonstrate process of collecting blood and blood products from the transfusion center.
Complete the completion of the independent double check process, patient monitoring time and documentation.
Demonstrate related pre, ongoing and post patient assessment during blood and blood products administration.
Discuss the role of the nurse and action to be taken when blood and plasma separate during administration.
Carry out the nurse's role and responsibilities when a reaction is identified including the immediate action to be taken, completion of the necessary reporting procedures and documentation required.
Demonstrate process when blood or blood products is collected from the transfusion center and then is returned because it's not used for any reasons.
Demonstrate the proper disposal of used blood and blood products transfusion set and blood bag.
attitude: Not be judgmental and accepts patient response and/or refusal for the administration of blood and blood products.
Ability of nurse to respond professionally and calmly if a reaction to the administration of blood and/ or blood products occurs.
To be self-aware of limitations in knowledge and skills and verbalizes these with nurse in charge.
To be approachable and open to answer patient and family's questions.
Attentive to overall patient experience e.g. pain, anxiety and have ability to provide comfort and emotional support needed.

Demonstrate ability to organize and facilitate a reflection session in and on practice after an administration of blood and/or blood products learning opportunity occurs and activate findings to improve future practice and response.

title: COMPLETING 12 LEAD ECG
knowledge: Explain the role and responsibilities of the nurse in completing a 12 lead ECG.
Discuss the placement of V1 to V6 chest leads and limb leads.
Discuss how to correctly prepare the skin for the electrode application e.g. wipe the skin with alcohol swabs and dry, shave the hair from the area and clean with alcohol swabs and dry.
Explain the importance of correct patient preparation prior to a 12 Lead ECG i.e. removal of jewelry and watches.
Explore the reasons that would necessitate calling the Physician to examine the patient due to a rhythm change e.g. explain the normal PQRST complex.
Explain how to document the procedure in patient notes correctly.
skills: Demonstrate the appropriate patient teaching and preparation for effective ECG results.
Perform a 12 Lead ECG correctly.
Demonstrate how to correctly prepare the skin for the electrode application e.g. wipe the skin with alcohol swabs and dry, shave the hair from the area and clean with alcohol swabs and dry.
Demonstrate the documentation of the procedure and completes relevant patient information to identify the completed 12 Lead ECG.
Demonstrate what the components of the by drawing a normal PQRST complex.
Demonstrate the appropriate patient teaching and preparation for effective ECG results.
attitude: To be self-aware of limitations in knowledge and skills and verbalize these with nurse in charge.
To be approachable and open to answer patient and family' questions.
Attentive to overall patient experience e.g. pain, anxiety and have ability to provide comfort and emotional support as needed.

Ability to organize and facilitate a reflection session in and on practice after an administration of 12 LEAD ECG learning opportunity occurs and activates findings to improve future practice and response.
